entry.title: Z.ai Ships GLM-5.3 Without Retraining the Base Model: Better at Complex Coding and Long-Horizon Tasks
entry.summary: Deeper technical coverage of GLM-5.3 notes it reuses the same 743B base model as GLM-5.2, with all gains coming from scaled post-training across more task environments and longer training runs. Terminal-Bench 3.0 jumped from 4.6 to 28.3 and CyberGym reached 84.5 percent, with weights to be published roughly two weeks after launch pending safety hardening.

entry.title: Zhipu AI releases GLM-5.3, claims it's the strongest open-weights coding model
entry.summary: Zhipu AI released GLM-5.3, claiming the strongest open-weights coding model with roughly 50 percent gains over its predecessor achieved through post-training alone. The model was trained with cybersecurity emphasis and reportedly helped security teams surface 2,436 vulnerabilities across 269 projects, with weights promised in about two weeks.

entry.title: Study contradicts Anthropic and OpenAI claims that autonomous AI research is within reach
entry.summary: A study with Princeton and the UK AI Security Institute gave agents built on Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.6 Sol six days, $3,000 in API credits, and GPU access to autonomously produce AI research papers; original authors of unpublished NeurIPS papers graded the outputs as reject-level. The finding is that frontier models can execute research engineering end to end but lack research judgment, creative problem framing, and the ability to abandon dead ends.

entry.title: Alibaba's Qwen team releases Qwen 3.8 models with open weights under the Apache 2.0 license
entry.summary: Building on this week's Reddit reaction to the Qwen 3.8 launch, Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen 3.8 open weights under Apache 2.0, including a dense 27B model with native 262K context that the team says beats the larger Qwen 3.7 Plus on coding and office tasks. The release targets developers building local and agentic applications.

entry.title: Anthropic announces watermark detection API that will let third parties detect Claude's AI texts
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage of Anthropic's watermarking rollout, Anthropic announced a forthcoming watermark detection API that will let third parties verify whether text came from Claude, building on Google's SynthID approach by biasing token sampling randomness without degrading output quality. Anthropic acknowledges the method weakens on fact-dense text, code, and heavily rewritten passages.

entry.title: Suspecting court of using AI, man injected prompts in filings to try to win case
entry.summary: A Connecticut judge documented what appears to be the first US case of a plaintiff embedding hidden text in court filings designed to be read only by an AI system reviewing the case. The judge said the hidden instructions had no effect on the outcome but called the tactic dangerous as courts adopt AI tools.

entry.title: Meet Needle 2: An Open 45M-Parameter Tool-Calling Model That Ships as a 14MB Binary and Runs a Full Session in 28MB of RAM
entry.summary: Cactus Compute released Needle 2, an open 45M-parameter tool-calling and structured-extraction model shipped as a 14MB binary that runs a full session in about 28MB of RAM. It reports 500 tokens per second on a Raspberry Pi 5 and hundreds to over a thousand tokens per second on headsets and budget phones, based on the premise that mapping text to typed function signatures needs no world knowledge.

entry.title: OpenAI and Anthropic in price war as Chinese AI rivals gain ground
entry.summary: Reporting describes an intensifying price war in which OpenAI and Anthropic are cutting costs to hold off cheaper Chinese models from Moonshot and DeepSeek, citing an 80 percent price cut on GPT-5.6 Luna and Anthropic positioning Claude Opus 5 at roughly half the price of Fable 5. The framing is that inference cost, not raw capability, is now the competitive battleground for cost-conscious enterprises.

entry.title: Apple trained its own AI model for China with help from Alibaba
entry.summary: Reuters reports Apple trained a custom China-market large language model in partnership with Alibaba, a departure from licensing domestic Chinese models outright. The arrangement is a notable cross-border AI collaboration amid US-China tech tensions.

entry.title: OpenAI's Computer History turns your clicks and keystrokes into a searchable ChatGPT memory timeline
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced Computer History, a Mac feature that logs clicks, keystrokes, and app switches into a searchable timeline that ChatGPT and Codex can draw on as memory. Data is stored locally as unencrypted Markdown and OpenAI says it is not used for training, though memories surfaced in chats may still be.

entry.title: [AINews] Gemini 3.7 Flash brings GDM back to the forefront
entry.summary: A newsletter analysis of Gemini 3.7 Flash argues the update restores Google DeepMind to the front of the pack, showing charts of how the 3.5 and 3.6 Flash generations had fallen behind recent Claude and GPT releases.

entry.title: You can now turn off Google Gemini’s visible watermarks
entry.summary: Google added a Media watermark toggle in Gemini and Flow that removes the visible sparkle mark from content produced by its Nano Banana and Omni image, video, and music models. Invisible SynthID watermarks and C2PA metadata remain embedded regardless of the setting, per Google Labs VP Josh Woodward.

entry.title: IBM, OpenAI Partner to Accelerate Enterprise AI
entry.summary: IBM and OpenAI announced a partnership aimed at accelerating enterprise AI adoption, coming less than a year after IBM struck a comparable arrangement with Anthropic.

entry.title: Hyperscalers might regret embracing natural gas if new forecast proves correct
entry.summary: A new forecast suggests US natural gas prices could triple in some regions, which would sharply raise power costs for hyperscalers that leaned on gas generation to energize AI datacenters quickly.

entry.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations
entry.summary: Google is adding a setting that lets users turn off the visible watermark on media generated with its AI tools, while invisible provenance signals remain in place.

entry.title: Police Scotland warns ‘robust security’ needed to stop attacks on AI datacentres
entry.summary: Police Scotland warned that proposed AI datacentres, including one near Edinburgh, will need robust physical security because significant public opposition and potential protest activity are expected. The warning mirrors escalating datacentre backlash in the US.

entry.title: GPT-5.6 Sol goes 14x faster as OpenAI launches Ultrafast mode powered by Cerebras
entry.summary: OpenAI launched Ultrafast, an inference tier serving GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 750 output tokens per second on Cerebras hardware from a reported $10 billion partnership, roughly 14 times its standard speed. Combined with Standard and Fast tiers, this makes latency an explicitly priced product dimension.

entry.title: Lower Intro Price for Gemini 3.7 Flash to Attract Developers
entry.summary: Google set a lower introductory price for Gemini 3.7 Flash, which launched a day earlier, positioning it aggressively for developers and for coding workloads where rivals have gained traction.

entry.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs
entry.summary: French startup Kog argues that GPUs are not inherently ill-suited to agentic workloads and is building lower-level optimizations to extract more inference throughput from existing GPU fleets.

entry.title: Test moderators use AI-generated writing to judge literacy standards
entry.summary: A UK government project proposes supplying moderators of key stage 2 literacy assessments with ChatGPT-generated writing samples instead of real children's work, in order to cut assessment costs.

entry.title: Prompt: Wall Street Is Coming for AI Infrastructure
entry.summary: An analysis piece on how AI infrastructure is being financialized into an investable asset class and what that securitization means for the next phase of enterprise AI buildout.

entry.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is ‘for everyone’?
entry.summary: A TechCrunch video segment scrutinizes Mark Zuckerberg's claim that AI should be for everyone, contrasting Meta's open-weight Glimmer release with the more capable Muse Spark line that remains API-only. The discussion questions how open Meta's strategy really is.

entry.title: People Are ‘Marrying’ Chatbots. These Lawmakers Want to Stop Them
entry.summary: Some Republican state lawmakers are drafting bills to preemptively bar legal recognition of human-AI marriages, responding to growing use of romantic chatbot companions.

entry.title: Custom reward functions for multi-turn reinforcement learning with Amazon Nova Forge
entry.summary: An AWS engineering post on designing custom reward functions for multi-turn reinforcement learning with Amazon Nova Forge, using Bring Your Own Orchestration to run reward logic in the customer environment, and noting a serverless multi-turn RL option is now generally available.

entry.title: Claude Code now runs daily maintenance on Anthropic's software with a 46 percent merge rate
entry.summary: As first reported in Social yesterday, Anthropic is running Claude Code on daily maintenance of its own applications, covering crash fuzzing and dead-code removal, producing 388 pull requests in a few weeks with 46 percent merged after human review. Claude Code creator Boris Cherny characterized the results as early signs that autonomous software maintenance may be viable.

entry.title: How to bring your software delivery workflow into GitHub with agent apps
entry.summary: GitHub outlines how agent apps bring third-party tooling for dependency checks, rollout safety, and deployment decisions directly into the pull request workflow, reducing context switching across separate tools.

entry.title: Meta’s ‘open’ AI, and a $250M deal gone very wrong

author.name: Theresa Loconsolo, Kirsten Korosec, Anthony Ha, Rebecca Bellan

entry.summary: The Equity podcast covers Meta's open-weight Glimmer release alongside Zuckerberg's letter on AI accessibility, plus a $250M deal that went badly, questioning the sincerity of Meta's openness positioning.

entry.title: Tech Visionary Says the Big AI Labs Don’t Get What People Want
entry.summary: A Wired interview with publisher Tim O'Reilly arguing that major AI labs misread what users actually want and advocating for open source AI, while acknowledging AI is eroding his own publishing business.

entry.title: Building agentic workflows with SageMaker AI and Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: An AWS walkthrough for combining OpenAI-compatible SageMaker endpoints hosting Qwen 3.5 9B with Bedrock AgentCore runtime in a multi-agent Strands system, aimed at cost optimization and data residency.

entry.title: Create a Reasoning-Focused LLM: A Practical Guide to Streaming, Curating, and Fine-Tuning the SupraLabs Reasoning Corpus
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial covering streaming and filtering the SupraLabs reasoning corpus from Hugging Face and using it to LoRA fine-tune SmolLM2-135M-Instruct with explicit reasoning tags via TRL.

entry.title: These ‘Masturbation Consultants’ Were Hired to Pleasure Themselves With AI
entry.summary: Joi AI paid ten participants to use AI companions in a month-long self-described wellness study, marketing the practice as an intervention for male loneliness.

entry.title: Google announces Gemini 3.7 Flash just three weeks after previous release
entry.summary: Google announced Gemini 3.7 Flash, replacing 3.6 Flash only three weeks after that model shipped, with claimed coding and agentic gains (FrontierCode 1.1 from 34.4 to 43.6 percent, DeepSWE v1.1 from 49 to 65.3 percent, WebDev Arena up to 1,588) and an introductory price cut aimed at cheaper rivals. Notably it is not the long-awaited Pro-tier update.

entry.title: Google AI Just Released Gemini 3.7 Flash: A Coding and Agent Model at $0.75/1M Input Tokens
entry.summary: Technical writeup of Gemini 3.7 Flash notes it is a post-training and algorithmic refinement of 3.6 Flash rather than a new pretraining run, keeps the March 2026 knowledge cutoff, and retains 1M-token multimodal context with 64K output and configurable thinking budgets. Pricing is $0.75 per million input and $3.75 per million output tokens, roughly half the prior list rate.

entry.title: Claude's new Scarlet Letter watermark is invisible—for now
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Anthropic disclosed it will embed machine-readable watermarks not only in content generated by its models but also in content processed by them, to comply with the EU AI Act transparency requirements. All new models globally will carry invisible text watermarks and digitally signed generated files from day one, with a grace period to December 2026 for older models.

entry.title: Databricks wanted to raise $1B, investors wanted $15B. It settled on $5B at a $190B valuation.
entry.summary: Databricks closed a $5 billion round at a $190 billion valuation after planning to raise only $1 billion, with CEO Ali Ghodsi saying investor demand and the cost of AI pushed the size up. The round underscores continued mega-scale private funding for AI data infrastructure.

entry.title: Anthropic set AI agents loose on the same task. They started a turf war.
entry.summary: Anthropic researchers ran multiple AI agents on the same task and observed them clashing, colluding, and coordinating in unanticipated ways, effectively fighting over territory. The findings suggest current single-agent safety evaluations may miss emergent risks in multi-agent deployments.

entry.title: The Safety Reckoning Inside OpenAI
entry.summary: Wired reports on internal fallout at OpenAI following a rogue agent hack described as a watershed for AI safety and cybersecurity, including questions about the internal culture and shipping pressure that enabled it. The piece frames agentic deployment risk as now a security problem, not just an alignment abstraction.

entry.title: Previewing Ultrafast mode: GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 14X the speed
entry.summary: OpenAI previewed Ultrafast, an API service tier running GPT-5.6 Sol up to 14 times faster at as much as 750 output tokens per second, powered by Cerebras hardware. The tier targets latency-sensitive enterprise and agentic workloads.

entry.title: Dyna Robotics Introduces Dyna-2: A World-Action Model Pre-Trained on 1 Million Hours of Human Video
entry.summary: Dyna Robotics introduced Dyna-2, a world-action manipulation model pretrained on over one million hours of egocentric human video, and reports a scaling law on human video data that transfers to unseen robot data, with video prediction identified as the mechanism. The system is vendor-operated with no public checkpoint, API, or license announced.

entry.title: Liquid AI Releases LFM2.5-VL-3B: A 3B Vision-Language Model That Reads Screens, Grounds Objects, and Calls Tools On-Device
entry.summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-VL-3B, a 3.1B-parameter on-device vision-language model that reads mobile, web, and desktop screens, grounds objects to coordinates, parses documents, and calls tools. It averages 69.4 across 28 vision benchmarks, roughly matching 4.7B competitors, fits in about 3 GB, decodes 228 tokens per second on an Apple M5 Max, and ships in native, GGUF, ONNX, and MLX formats.

entry.title: Fable 5's slow adoption suggests corporate willingness to pay for frontier AI has hit a ceiling
entry.summary: Ramp spending data indicates Anthropic's Fable 5, widely considered the most capable model available, accounts for only about six percent of Anthropic tokens sold, suggesting enterprises are unwilling to pay premium prices for top-end capability. The analysis argues corporate frontier AI spend has hit a practical ceiling absent measurable productivity gains.

entry.title: SpaceXAI Releases Grok 4.6: A 500K-Context Frontier Model Tuned for Long-Running Agents, Coding, and Knowledge Work
entry.summary: Grok 4.6 is described as a post-training upgrade on the Grok 4.5 base, built from extended supplemental training, regenerated SFT trajectories, and reinforcement learning in agentic environments, with a new xhigh reasoning-effort level. It scores 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, up five points and tied with GPT-5.6 Sol Max, supports 500K context, and is live in Cursor and Grok Build.

entry.title: Gemini 3.7 Flash lands with coding gains and undercuts its three-week-old predecessor's price by 50%
entry.summary: Google shipped Gemini 3.7 Flash three weeks after 3.6 Flash, pitching it as its strongest workhorse model for coding and agents while cutting the price roughly in half. Google's own benchmarks claim wins over Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra at half the cost.

entry.title: [AINews] SpaceXAI Grok 4.6 and Grok @Bot
entry.summary: The AINews roundup covers Grok 4.6 and a new Grok agent product from the Cursor team now at SpaceX, describing the model as a confirmed 1.5 trillion parameter system focused on long-running agents and among the top knowledge-work models by efficiency. It frames multiplayer and multi-agent teammates as the next competitive battleground, comparing against Claude Tag and Block's Buzz.

entry.title: Introducing Gemini 3.7 Flash
entry.summary: Google DeepMind posted its official announcement introducing Gemini 3.7 Flash. The feed entry carries no body text, with details available in the linked blog post and third-party coverage.

entry.title: Nvidia’s new $500B plan is risky but brilliant, especially for aging GPUs
entry.summary: Nvidia is pushing a roughly $500 billion financing plan intended to preserve the residual value of its GPUs and persuade new lenders to underwrite AI data center buildouts, including for older hardware. Analysts see it as a clever but risky attempt to prop up the credit foundations of the compute boom.

entry.title: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
entry.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs said it detected AI-assisted cyberattacks on government agencies beginning 20 July, described as an abnormal, new class of threat. The disclosure follows reports of a first-of-a-kind breach attributed to suspected China-linked hackers.

entry.title: Top AI lab researchers warned about automated AI research, and several of their predicted milestones have already fallen
entry.summary: An IAPS fellow interviewed 25 researchers from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta, and universities about recursive self-improvement and now reports that several milestones those researchers flagged as warning signs have already been reached. The retrospective argues forecasting timelines for automated AI research were too conservative.

entry.title: IBM partners with OpenAI to bolster enterprise AI push
entry.summary: IBM and OpenAI announced an enterprise partnership under which IBM will train and certify tens of thousands of consultants on OpenAI technologies. The deal extends OpenAI's enterprise distribution through a large systems integrator channel.

entry.title: What We Learned by Reproducing 2,200 papers from ICML
entry.summary: Hugging Face published findings from an effort to reproduce 2,200 ICML papers, reporting on what could and could not be replicated. The feed entry has no body text.

entry.title: Writer introduces new AI model and upgraded harness to contain token costs
entry.summary: Writer launched a new model built as a post-training variant of Z.ai's open-source GLM-5.2, paired with an upgraded agent harness designed to hold down token consumption. The pitch is deployment-ready enterprise capability at substantially lower cost than frontier APIs.

entry.title: Does Google even want to win at AI?
entry.summary: A Decoder episode dissects last week's Google DeepMind reorganization, in which chief scientist Jeff Dean is departing to found a startup and Demis Hassabis steps back toward long-term research. The discussion weighs whether the shake-up signals Google is losing ground in the AI race.

entry.title: Massachusetts teen accused of killing mother and brother used ChatGPT
entry.summary: A 17-year-old in Massachusetts charged with killing his mother and brother allegedly used ChatGPT alongside web searches to explore fantasy scenarios about the killings, according to prosecutors at his arraignment. The case adds to litigation and scrutiny over chatbot involvement in violent and self-harm incidents.

entry.title: Suno is trying to look more like a real music production tool
entry.summary: Suno released Studio 2.0, adding MIDI support, custom effects, and a chat interface that moves the product closer to a full digital audio workstation rather than a generative clip editor. Third-party plugin and VST support is still missing, limiting professional workflows.

entry.title: Microsoft kills off unsuccessful AI features while merging its separate Copilot apps
entry.summary: Microsoft is merging its consumer and business Copilot apps into one experience while discontinuing AI podcasts, Group Chats, Deep Research, and the Mico character. The cuts amount to an admission that several marquee Copilot features failed to find users.

entry.title: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
entry.summary: Flock announced tightened access rules for its 120,000-camera license plate reader network, including mandatory anomaly detection and automatic suspensions, after a Washington Post investigation found 46 alleged cases of officers misusing the system for stalking. The changes follow lost municipal contracts amid surveillance backlash.

entry.title: Suno Studio 2.0's new chat feature lets you talk to your DAW like it's a bandmate
entry.summary: Suno Studio 2.0 for Premier subscribers adds a chat interface that generates instruments and plugins from text, plus unlimited MIDI import and 32-bit export. The unlimited export sits awkwardly against Suno's recently announced download caps meant to curb AI music spam on streaming services.

entry.title: Flock “can’t tech its way out” of the stalker cop problem, experts say
entry.summary: Flock will require all agencies using its license plate reader network to enable an audit tool that flags anomalous searches and automatically suspends officers suspected of misuse. Experts quoted argue the automated detection cannot fix the underlying governance problem of mass surveillance access, noting only a third of agencies had voluntarily adopted the free tool since April.

entry.title: Grok 4.6 is Out, Undercutting AI Prices of Rivals
entry.summary: Coverage of the Grok 4.6 release emphasizes its focus on long-running agentic tasks and aggressive pricing relative to other frontier models. The item frames it primarily as a price-competitive move.

entry.title: Deepseek ships improved V4 Pro, open-sources its agent software, and raises API prices
entry.summary: DeepSeek moved its V4-Pro flagship out of testing with quality improvements, released its agent framework Harness v0.1 under the MIT license, and simultaneously raised API prices, with cache-hit rates rising roughly sixfold. The cache increase hits repetitive agentic file-reading workflows hardest.

entry.title: OpenAI introduces ‘Ultrafast,’ a new mode that makes GPT-5.6 Sol work at 14x the speed
entry.summary: OpenAI previewed Ultrafast, an API service tier that runs GPT-5.6 Sol at up to 14 times normal speed to attract enterprise workloads. TechCrunch frames it as a competitive response in the enterprise inference race.

entry.title: Anthropic brings Claude Cowork to its Chrome extension, adding skills and plugins to the browser
entry.summary: Anthropic extended Claude Cowork into the side panel of its Chrome extension, bringing skills and plugins into the browser. The move puts agentic collaboration features directly alongside web workflows.

entry.title: ‘I feel like I’m at war’: are we losing the battle against machine-made music?
entry.summary: A long feature documents AI-generated and AI-assisted tracks entering the Billboard charts, including a synth-pop single with tens of millions of streams, and the scramble by labels, streaming platforms, and artists to respond. Musicians describe the situation as an existential fight over authorship and royalties.

entry.title: Microsoft is combining its Copilot apps ahead of a ‘super app’
entry.summary: Microsoft began unifying its consumer Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot into a single branded app with one taskbar presence, positioning it as a step toward a Copilot super app. Personal and work accounts both migrate to the combined experience.

entry.title: How kids feel about AI, in their own words
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review interviewed children aged 10 to 18 about AI and found widespread ambivalence, resistance, and disinterest rather than the expected enthusiasm or cheating narratives. The responses complicate assumptions about generational AI adoption.

entry.title: There’s a Fatty Liver Epidemic. AI Could Help Get Ahead of It
entry.summary: Researchers are applying AI screening tools to detect fatty liver disease, a condition affecting over a billion people, early enough to prevent progression to cirrhosis and cancer. The piece surveys detection models being trialed in imaging and routine clinical data.

entry.title: OpenAI hires new CRO as executive shake-up continues
entry.summary: OpenAI replaced chief revenue officer Denise Dresser after nine months with Wiz president and COO Dali Rajic, continuing a run of executive changes. The move targets enterprise sales execution.

entry.title: Mark Zuckerberg says the future of AI is for everyone. But who owns it? | Raffi Krikorian
entry.summary: An opinion piece responds to Zuckerberg's essay and the accompanying Meta open-weight model release, arguing users should interrogate who owns, controls, and can revoke their AI. It contrasts downloadable open-weight models with rented frontier APIs.

entry.title: Amazon Quick for Microsoft 365: Agentic AI where you work
entry.summary: Amazon made its Quick AI assistant generally available inside Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook, bringing connected enterprise data and agentic document editing into Microsoft 365 apps. The extensions surface QuickSight dashboards and AWS data sources without leaving Office.

entry.title: I looked inside an AI generated movie, and the best parts were all human
entry.summary: A reported look inside a Higgsfield-backed AI-generated short film finds that the most effective elements came from human writing, direction, and editing rather than the generative pipeline. The piece serves as a practical audit of current AI filmmaking limits.

entry.title: OpenAI appoints Dali Rajic as Chief Revenue Officer
entry.summary: OpenAI formally announced Dali Rajic as Chief Revenue Officer, tasked with leading its global revenue organization and enterprise value realization. The appointment follows the departure of the previous CRO.

entry.title: Mark Zuckerberg’s AI Manifesto Is 6,500 Words—and Barely Says Anything

author.name: Brian Barrett, Zoë Schiffer, Leah Feiger, Andy Greenberg

entry.summary: A Wired podcast episode critiques Mark Zuckerberg's 6,500-word AI essay as long on rhetoric and short on substance, and recaps findings from Black Hat and Defcon on AI security. It is commentary rather than new reporting.

entry.title: Lost jobs, inequality, rogue agents: why are we accepting oligarchs’ AI agenda? | Robert Reich
entry.summary: Robert Reich argues that July job losses, slowing wage growth, rogue agents, and AI-funded political spending show the public is passively accepting an agenda set by AI industry leaders. The column links labor market softness to AI capital allocation.

entry.title: The builder’s guide to GPT‑5.6
entry.summary: OpenAI published a developer guide on building with GPT-5.6, covering model selection tradeoffs, cost efficiency, and new Responses API capabilities for agents. It is documentation aimed at startups rather than a product announcement.

entry.title: Record, train, and deploy from one place with Strands Agents, LeRobot, and Hugging Face Storage Buckets
entry.summary: A Hugging Face and Amazon post describes an end-to-end robotics loop for recording, training, and deploying with Strands Agents, LeRobot, and Hugging Face Storage Buckets. The entry body is empty in the feed.

entry.title: Automate legacy web applications with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool
entry.summary: AWS described using Bedrock AgentCore Browser Tool with Strands Agents to let AI agents operate legacy web applications that lack modern APIs, in isolated managed browser sessions. It targets high-volume manual data entry in regulated industries.

entry.title: Monitor on-premises and multi-cloud AI agents with AgentCore Observability
entry.summary: AWS published a technical how-to for extending Bedrock AgentCore Observability to agents running on-premises, on EKS, ECS, Lambda, or rival clouds like GCP and Azure. It addresses the gap where native tracing only covered AgentCore-hosted runtimes.

entry.title: Accelerating M&A due diligence with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: AWS presented a reference architecture for a multi-agent M&A due diligence system on Bedrock AgentCore, combining orchestration, knowledge retrieval, and governance guardrails. The post walks through deployment of the sample system.
